source.text: ה֗וֹי עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְצִ֥יץ נֹבֵ֖ל צְבִ֣י תִפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֛ר עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ גֵּֽיא־שְׁמָנִ֖ים הֲל֥וּמֵי יָֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe, [the] crown of pride of [the] drunkards of Ephraim, and [the] flower fading, [the] beauty of its splendor, which [is] on [the] head of [the] valley of fatness of [those] struck down [by] wine!

en.L: Woe, the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim, and the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which [is] on [the] head of [the] valley of richness of [those] struck down [by] wine!
en.B: Woe to the proud garland of Ephraim's drunkards, to the wilting blossom of its splendid beauty, set at the head of the fertile valley of those laid low by wine!
en.R: How terrible it will be for Samaria, the proud crown of the drunken people of Israel's northern kingdom! It sits at the top of a rich valley. But its beauty is like a flower that is drying up. Its people have been knocked down by wine.

decisions.choice: the crown on the head of the valley: Samaria, capital of Ephraim, the northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Samaria stood on a rounded hill above a fertile valley, ringed by its walls like a crown or a garland on a head. Ephraim, the largest northern tribe, stands for the whole northern kingdom (7:2; 9:8). Assyria took Samaria in 722 BC, so this oracle dates from before that fall.

decisions.choice: crown, fading flower: a wreath of flowers worn at a drinking feast, already wilting
alternatives: a royal crown
decisions.reason: Revelers wore garlands of flowers at banquets. The proud city is pictured as the wreath on a drunkard's head, beautiful for a moment and already withering (40:7-8).

decisions.choice: struck down by wine: overcome by drink
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a blow that knocks someone down (16:8, of vines). Wine has beaten them as an enemy would.

decisions.choice: Samaria; Israel's northern kingdom
decisions.reason: Readable names the city the crown stands for and explains Ephraim (see m1).

source.text: הִנֵּ֨ה חָזָ֤ק וְאַמִּץ֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔י כְּזֶ֥רֶם בָּרָ֖ד שַׂ֣עַר קָ֑טֶב כְּ֠זֶרֶם מַ֣יִם כַּבִּירִ֥ים שֹׁטְפִ֛ים הִנִּ֥יחַ לָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, [one] mighty and strong [belongs] to [the] Lord, like a storm of hail, a tempest of destruction, like a storm of waters mighty, overflowing, he has thrust [it] down to [the] ground with [the] hand.

en.L: Look, [one] mighty and strong [belongs] to the Lord, like a storm of hail, a tempest of destruction, like a storm of mighty waters overflowing; he will throw [it] down to the ground with [the] hand.
en.B: Look, the Lord holds ready one who is mighty and powerful. Like a storm of hail and a wrecking wind, like a downpour of great waters that sweep all before them, he will dash it to the ground by force.
en.R: Look! The Lord has someone strong and powerful ready to attack. He will come like a hailstorm and a destroying wind, like a heavy rain that floods everything. He will throw Samaria's crown to the ground with great force.

decisions.choice: one mighty and strong belonging to the Lord: the Assyrian king and his army, God's instrument
alternatives: the Lord himself
decisions.reason: The figure is not named. Isaiah elsewhere pictures Assyria as a flood sent by the Lord (8:7-8) and as the rod in God's hand (10:5). The storm and flood here fit that picture.

decisions.choice: with the hand: with force
decisions.reason: The bare phrase "with hand" means by sheer strength. What is thrown down is the crown of verse 1.

decisions.choice: ready to attack; Samaria's crown
decisions.reason: Readable says why the strong one is ready and names what he throws down (verses 1 and 3).

source.text: בְּרַגְלַ֖יִם תֵּֽרָמַ֑סְנָה עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: With feet they will be trampled, [the] crown of pride of [the] drunkards of Ephraim.

en.L: With feet it will be trampled, the crown of pride of the drunkards of Ephraim.
en.B: The proud garland of Ephraim's drunkards will be trodden underfoot.
en.R: Enemies will walk all over Samaria, the proud crown of Israel's drunken people.

decisions.choice: trampled underfoot: utter humiliation of a conquered city
decisions.reason: A crown thrown to the ground and stamped on pictures a city captured and shamed (25:10; 26:6).

decisions.choice: Enemies; Samaria
decisions.reason: Readable names who tramples and what the crown stands for (verse 1).

source.text: וְֽהָ֨יְתָ֜ה צִיצַ֤ת נֹבֵל֙ צְבִ֣י תִפְאַרְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹ֖אשׁ גֵּ֣יא שְׁמָנִ֑ים כְּבִכּוּרָהּ֙בְּטֶ֣רֶם קַ֔יִץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְאֶ֤ה הָֽרֹאֶה֙ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּעוֹדָ֥הּ בְּכַפּ֖וֹ יִבְלָעֶֽנָּה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And it will be [the] flower fading, [the] beauty of its splendor, which [is] on [the] head of [the] valley of fatness, like an early fig before summer, which [he] sees [it], the one seeing, while still it [is] in his palm, he swallows it.

en.L: And the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which [is] on [the] head of [the] valley of richness, will be like a first-ripe fig before summer, which the one who sees [it] sees; while it [is] still in his palm, he swallows it.
en.B: And the wilting blossom of its splendid beauty, set at the head of the fertile valley, will be like the first fig that ripens before summer: someone catches sight of it, and before it has left his hand, he has eaten it.
en.R: Samaria's beauty at the top of the rich valley is fading like a dying flower. It will be like the first fig of the season. Anyone who sees it grabs it and eats it right away. In the same way, the enemy will quickly swallow up the city.

decisions.choice: an early fig before summer: the first fig of the year, eaten the moment it is found
decisions.reason: A few figs ripen in early summer, before the main harvest, and were prized (Hosea 9:10; Micah 7:1). No one saves such a fig; it is picked and eaten at once. So Samaria will be taken quickly and completely.

decisions.choice: the one who sees it ... swallows it: whoever finds it eats it at once
decisions.reason: The same root "swallow" returns in verse 7, where the leaders of Judah are "swallowed up" by wine.

decisions.choice: In the same way, the enemy will quickly swallow up the city.
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the picture; the enemy is the strong one of verse 2.

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י וְלִצְפִירַ֖ת תִּפְאָרָ֑ה לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: In the day the that will be Yahweh of hosts for a crown of beauty and for a diadem of splendor for [the] remnant of his people,

en.L: In that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts will be for a crown of beauty and for a diadem of splendor to the remnant of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people,
en.B: On that day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will be the splendid crown, the beautiful garland, worn by the survivors of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people,
en.R: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} will be like a beautiful crown for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people who are left.

decisions.choice: the LORD as crown: God himself replaces the fading crown of pride
decisions.reason: The words "crown", "beauty" and "splendor" from verses 1 and 4 return. Samaria's proud wreath withers, but the LORD becomes the glory of those who are left (4:2; 62:3).

decisions.choice: the remnant: those of God's people who survive the judgment
decisions.reason: A key idea in Isaiah (10:20-22; 11:11, 16), named in the name of his son Shear-jashub, "a remnant will return" (7:3).

decisions.choice: himself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "himself" to bring out the contrast with Samaria's crown.

source.text: וּלְר֖וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט לַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־הַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְלִ֨גְבוּרָ֔ה מְשִׁיבֵ֥י מִלְחָמָ֖ה שָֽׁעְרָה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: and for a spirit of justice for the [one who] sits over the judgment, and for strength [for those who] turn back battle at the gate.

en.L: and for a spirit of justice to the [one who] sits over the judgment, and for strength [to those who] turn back battle [at the] gate.
en.B: the spirit of justice in the one who presides over the court, and the strength of those who hurl the attack back at the gate.
en.R: He will help judges to be fair. He will give strength to soldiers who drive enemies back at the city gate.

decisions.choice: a spirit of justice: the power to judge rightly, given by God
decisions.reason: As with the king of 11:2-4, God's spirit enables right judgment. Here the LORD himself is that spirit for the judge.

decisions.choice: those who turn back the battle at the gate: defenders who drive the attackers away from the city gate
alternatives: those who drive the battle back to the enemy's gate
decisions.reason: The last word means "to the gate" or "at the gate". It may picture defenders pushing the enemy back from their own gate, or pursuing them back to the enemy's gate.

decisions.choice: judges; soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant: the one who sits in judgment and the fighters at the gate.

source.text: וְגַם־אֵ֨לֶּה֙ בַּיַּ֣יִן שָׁג֔וּ וּבַשֵּׁכָ֖ר תָּע֑וּ כֹּהֵ֣ן וְנָבִיא֩ שָׁג֨וּ בַשֵּׁכָ֜ר נִבְלְע֣וּ מִן־הַיַּ֗יִן תָּעוּ֙ מִן־הַשֵּׁכָ֔ר שָׁגוּ֙ בָּֽרֹאֶ֔ה פָּק֖וּ פְּלִילִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And also these with wine they reel and with strong drink they stagger; priest and prophet they reel with strong drink, they are swallowed from the wine, they stagger from the strong drink, they reel in the vision, they totter [in] decision.

en.L: And these also reel with wine and stagger with strong drink; priest and prophet reel with strong drink; they are swallowed up by wine; they stagger from strong drink; they reel in vision; they totter [in] judgment.
en.B: Yet these too sway with wine and lurch with beer. Priest and prophet sway with beer and are swallowed up by wine. They lurch from beer, sway as they see visions, and totter when they hand down a ruling.
en.R: But the leaders of Judah also stumble around because of wine and beer. Priests and prophets are drunk on beer. Wine has swallowed them up. They stagger because of beer. They stumble while they are seeing visions. They stumble when they decide cases.

decisions.choice: these also: the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem, as drunk as Ephraim's
alternatives: the drunkards of Ephraim, described further
decisions.reason: After the northern kingdom (verses 1-4), the prophet turns to the leaders near him. Verse 14 names them: the rulers in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: strong drink: beer, the fermented drink made from grain
decisions.reason: The word is paired with wine throughout the Old Testament (5:11, 22; 24:9) and covers fermented drink other than wine, chiefly barley beer. The same word is used in the settled wording of 5:11.

decisions.choice: swallowed up by wine; reel in vision, totter in judgment
decisions.reason: "Swallowed up" can also mean "confused"; the word echoes the fig swallowed in verse 4. The prophet should see visions and the priest give rulings (Deuteronomy 17:9; Ezekiel 44:24); both duties are done while drunk.

decisions.choice: beer
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "beer" for the grain drink, as at 5:11 and 24:9; Literal keeps "strong drink".

decisions.choice: the leaders of Judah
decisions.reason: Readable names who "these" are (m1).

source.text: כִּ֚י כָּל־שֻׁלְחָנ֔וֹת מָלְא֖וּ קִ֣יא צֹאָ֑ה בְּלִ֖י מָקֽוֹם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For all tables they are full [of] vomit, filth, without place.

en.L: For all [the] tables are full [of] vomit, filth, without [a] place [left].
en.B: Every table is smeared with vomit; there is filth everywhere, and no clean place.
en.R: Every table is covered with vomit and filth. There is not one clean place left.

decisions.choice: filth: excrement
decisions.reason: The word means human excrement (36:12 uses a related word). The feast of the leaders ends in disgusting squalor.

source.text: אֶת־מִי֙ יוֹרֶ֣ה דֵעָ֔ה וְאֶת־מִ֖י יָבִ֣ין שְׁמוּעָ֑ה גְּמוּלֵי֙ מֵֽחָלָ֔ב עַתִּיקֵ֖י מִשָּׁדָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: Whom will he teach knowledge, and whom will he make understand [the] message? [Those] weaned from milk, [those] removed from [the] breasts?

en.L: Whom will he teach knowledge, and whom will he make understand [the] message? [Those] weaned from milk, [those] taken from [the] breasts?
en.B: Who does he imagine he is teaching? Who needs his lessons explained? Babies just off milk, newly taken from the breast?
en.R: The leaders make fun of me and say, "Who does this prophet think he is teaching? Who is he explaining his message to? Babies who have just stopped nursing?

decisions.choice: whom will he teach: the drunken leaders mocking the prophet
alternatives: the prophet asking who can still be taught
decisions.reason: Verses 9-10 are best read as the scornful words of the priests and prophets of verse 7: Isaiah treats them like small children. Verse 14 calls them "scoffers". The verses could instead be the prophet's own question about who is left to teach, if not little children.

decisions.choice: message: what is heard, a report
decisions.reason: The word means something heard. It returns in verse 19, where understanding the message brings terror.

decisions.choice: The leaders make fun of me and say
decisions.reason: Readable names the speakers and marks their words as a quotation, which runs to the end of verse 10 (m1).

source.text: כִּ֣י צַ֤ו לָצָו֙ צַ֣ו לָצָ֔ו קַ֥ו לָקָ֖ו קַ֣ו לָקָ֑ו זְעֵ֥יר שָׁ֖ם זְעֵ֥יר שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: For tsav latsav tsav latsav, qav laqav qav laqav, a little there, a little there.

en.L: For [it is] tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav, a little there, a little there.
en.B: It is all tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav, a little here, a little there!
en.R: All he says is tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav, a little here, a little there. It sounds like baby talk!"

decisions.choice: tsav latsav, qav laqav: repeated sounds that mock the prophet's teaching as baby talk
alternatives: command on command, command on command, line on line, line on line
letters of the alphabet recited in a lesson
decisions.reason: The words are short, rhyming syllables, repeated like a nursery chant. They may be nonsense sounds, the babble of a small child. They may be the names of two letters of the alphabet drilled in a child's lessons. Or they may be real words: tsav is close to "command" and qav means "measuring line", so "command on command, line on line". The sound is the point, and it is kept at every level. The same syllables return in verse 13, where God turns the mockery back on the speakers, and qav returns in verse 17 as God's measuring line.

decisions.choice: a little there, a little there: bit by bit, as children are taught
decisions.reason: The phrase pictures a lesson given in small pieces, scorned as fit only for infants.

decisions.choice: tsav latsav, qav laqav (sounds kept)
alternatives: precept upon precept, line upon line
decisions.reason: The syllables are written out in letters so the reader hears the chant. A translation into words ("command on command") would lose the mockery; it is given in the footnote (m1).

decisions.choice: All he says is ...; It sounds like baby talk!
decisions.reason: Readable continues the leaders' quotation from verse 9 and states the point of the chant (m1).

source.text: כִּ֚י בְּלַעֲגֵ֣י שָׂפָ֔ה וּבְלָשׁ֖וֹן אַחֶ֑רֶת יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For with stammerings of lip and with a tongue other he will speak to the people the this,

en.L: For with stammerings of lip and with another tongue {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will speak to this people,
en.B: Indeed, with halting speech and in a foreign language {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will speak to this people,
en.R: So now God will speak to these people through foreigners who talk in a language they cannot understand.

decisions.choice: stammering lips and another tongue: the speech of foreign invaders
decisions.reason: Since the leaders call God's message babble, God will speak to them in a language that really is babble to them: the speech of the Assyrian army (33:19; Deuteronomy 28:49). Judgment comes in a tongue they cannot follow.

decisions.choice: quoted in 1 Corinthians 14:21
decisions.reason: Paul quotes this verse, freely, to say that speaking in unknown tongues is a sign for unbelievers rather than a means of persuading them, much as the foreign speech here was a sign of judgment on a people who would not listen.

decisions.choice: God; through foreigners
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and says how he speaks (m1).

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀אָמַ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם זֹ֤את הַמְּנוּחָה֙ הָנִ֣יחוּ לֶֽעָיֵ֔ף וְזֹ֖את הַמַּרְגֵּעָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וּא שְׁמֽוֹעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: to whom he said, This [is] the rest, give rest to the weary, and this [is] the repose; and not they were willing to hear.

en.L: to whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "This [is] the rest; give rest to the weary; and this [is] the place of repose," but they were not willing to hear.
en.B: to whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} once said, "Here is rest: give the weary rest. Here is relief." But they refused to hear it.
en.R: He had told them, "This is the place where you can rest. Let tired people rest. This is where you will find relief." But they refused to listen.

decisions.choice: rest, repose: the security God offered to those who trusted him
alternatives: the land as God's resting place for his people
decisions.reason: God had offered his people quiet safety in their land if they relied on him rather than on alliances and armies (7:4, 9; 30:15). The leaders turned it down; now they will hear foreign speech instead (verse 11).

decisions.choice: they refused to hear it
decisions.reason: The verb means they were not willing; "refused" says this plainly.

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם דְּבַר־יְהוָ֗ה צַ֣ו לָצָ֞ו צַ֤ו לָצָו֙ קַ֤ו לָקָו֙ קַ֣ו לָקָ֔ו זְעֵ֥יר שָׁ֖ם זְעֵ֣יר שָׁ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן יֵלְכ֜וּ וְכָשְׁל֤וּ אָחוֹר֙ וְנִשְׁבָּ֔רוּ וְנוֹקְשׁ֖וּ וְנִלְכָּֽדוּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And it will be to them [the] word of Yahweh tsav latsav tsav latsav, qav laqav qav laqav, a little there, a little there, so that they may go and they will stumble backward and they will be broken and they will be snared and they will be captured.

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be to them tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav, a little there, a little there, so that they will go and stumble backward, and be broken, and be snared, and be captured.
en.B: So the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will come to them as tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav, a little here, a little there, so that they will walk on and fall backward, broken, trapped, and taken captive.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s message to them will sound like babble: tsav latsav, tsav latsav, qav laqav, qav laqav, a little here, a little there. Then they will go out and fall backward. They will be hurt, trapped, and captured.

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD will be tsav latsav to them: the mockery turned back on the mockers
decisions.reason: The leaders called the prophet's message baby talk (verse 10). Now God's word will come to them exactly as they described it: incomprehensible, in the foreign speech of verse 11. See the note at verse 10 on the sounds.

decisions.choice: stumble, be broken, be snared, be captured: the same doom as 8:15
decisions.reason: The four verbs repeat 8:14-15, where the LORD is a stone that makes both houses of Israel stumble. The stone returns in verse 16.

decisions.choice: so that: the result God intends
decisions.reason: The conjunction expresses purpose or result. As in 6:9-10, refusing God's word leads to hardening and judgment.

decisions.choice: will sound like babble
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of repeating the chant (m1).

source.text: לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן מֹֽשְׁלֵי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore hear [the] word of Yahweh, men of scoffing, rulers of the people the this who [are] in Jerusalem.

en.L: Therefore hear [the] word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, men of scorn, rulers of this people who [are] in Jerusalem!
en.B: Now then, you men who sneer, you who govern this people in Jerusalem: listen to what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says!
en.R: You leaders in Jerusalem who mock, listen now to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s message!

decisions.choice: men of scorn: scoffers, those who mock what is holy
decisions.reason: In the wisdom books the scoffer is the one who will not be taught (Proverbs 1:22; 9:7-8). The word picks up the mocking of verses 9-10.

decisions.choice: rulers: those who govern, with a possible play on "makers of sayings"
alternatives: those who make proverbs about this people
decisions.reason: The same letters can mean "rule" or "make a proverb, a taunt". The leaders who rule are also the ones who coin mocking sayings like verse 10 and the boast of verse 15.

source.text: כִּ֣י אֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם כָּרַ֤תְנֽוּ בְרִית֙ אֶת־מָ֔וֶת וְעִם־שְׁא֖וֹל עָשִׂ֣ינוּ חֹזֶ֑ה שׁ֣וֹט שׁוֹטֵ֤ף כִּֽי־יַֽעֲבֹר֙ לֹ֣א יְבוֹאֵ֔נוּ כִּ֣י שַׂ֧מְנוּ כָזָ֛ב מַחְסֵ֖נוּ וּבַשֶּׁ֥קֶר נִסְתָּֽרְנוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: For you have said, We have cut a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made an agreement; [the] scourge overflowing, when it passes through, not it will come to us; for we have made lie our refuge, and in the falsehood we have hidden ourselves.

en.L: For you have said, "We have cut a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made a pact; [the] overflowing whip, when it passes through, will not come to us, for we have made a lie our refuge, and in falsehood we have hidden ourselves."
en.B: For you have said, "We have made a covenant with death; we have a pact with Sheol. When the flooding whip sweeps through, it will not reach us, for we have taken shelter in a lie and hidden ourselves inside falsehood."
en.R: You have said, "We have made an agreement with death. We have a deal with the grave. When disaster floods through the land like a whip, it will not touch us. Our lies will keep us safe. Our tricks will hide us."

decisions.choice: a covenant with death, a pact with Sheol: a treaty the leaders trusted to keep them from destruction
alternatives: a treaty with Egypt
rites to win protection from the powers of death
decisions.reason: The leaders boast of an agreement that will protect them when the invader floods the land. Isaiah gives it a mocking name. It most likely means their alliance with Egypt against Assyria (30:1-3; 31:1), bound by oaths before gods. It may also hint at seeking help from the dead or from the god of death (8:19). Either way, what they thought protected them from death was a bargain with death itself.

decisions.choice: pact: an agreement
decisions.reason: The word is normally "seer" or "vision". Here, parallel to "covenant", it means a binding agreement, perhaps one confirmed by a seer's word. It returns in verse 18.

decisions.choice: whip; passes through: the qere
decisions.reason: The written consonants have a different spelling of "whip" and a past form, "passed through"; the scribes' marginal reading gives "whip" in its usual spelling and a future, "will pass through", as in verse 18. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the flooding whip; a lie, falsehood
decisions.reason: Two pictures of Assyria are joined: the flood of 8:7-8 and the whip of 10:26. The leaders would not have called their shelter "a lie"; the prophet puts his verdict on their plan into their own mouths.

decisions.choice: agreement; the grave
decisions.reason: Readable says "agreement" for covenant and "the grave" for Sheol (settled wording).

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֛י יִסַּ֥ד בְּצִיּ֖וֹן אָ֑בֶן אֶ֣בֶן בֹּ֜חַן פִּנַּ֤ת יִקְרַת֙ מוּסָ֣ד מוּסָּ֔ד הַֽמַּאֲמִ֖ין לֹ֥א יָחִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Look, I [am the one who] has laid in Zion a stone, a stone of testing, a corner of preciousness of a foundation founded; the [one who] trusts not he will hurry.

en.L: Therefore thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Look, I [am the one who] has laid in Zion a stone, a stone of testing, a precious corner[stone] of a foundation firmly founded; the [one who] trusts will not hurry.
en.B: So the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Look, I have laid a stone in Zion as its foundation: a stone proven by testing, a valuable cornerstone, set deep and secure. The one who trusts will not rush in panic.
en.R: So this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Look! I have set a stone in Zion as a foundation. It is a stone that has been tested. It is a valuable cornerstone that holds the building firm. Anyone who trusts will not panic and run.

decisions.choice: a tested, precious cornerstone in Zion: what God himself has founded, in contrast to the leaders' shelter of lies
decisions.reason: Against the false refuge of verse 15, God sets a true foundation in Zion. The stone stands for what God has established there: his promise to Zion and to David's line (2 Samuel 7:16; Isaiah 8:14; 14:32), to be received by trust (7:9). The New Testament applies the verse to Jesus as the cornerstone (Romans 9:33; 1 Peter 2:6; compare Ephesians 2:20).

decisions.choice: I am the one who has laid: a completed act
alternatives: I am laying
I will lay
decisions.reason: Hebrew reads "Look, I, he has laid", a relative clause: God is the one who laid the stone. The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsa-a) is reported to read a participle, "I am laying", and the Septuagint has a future, "I will lay". The received text is kept.

decisions.choice: will not hurry: will not run in panic
alternatives: will not be put to shame (Septuagint)
decisions.reason: The verb means to hurry. The one who trusts will stay calm and not flee in alarm (compare 30:15-16). The Septuagint has "will not be put to shame", and Romans 9:33; 10:11 and 1 Peter 2:6 quote that form. Neither "trusts" nor "hurry" has a stated object; the context implies trust in God and in what he has founded.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ לְקָ֔ו וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְמִשְׁקָ֑לֶת וְיָעָ֤ה בָרָד֙ מַחְסֵ֣ה כָזָ֔ב וְסֵ֥תֶר מַ֖יִם יִשְׁטֹֽפוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will make justice for a line and righteousness for a level, and it will sweep away hail [the] refuge of lie, and [the] hiding place waters they will overflow.

en.L: And I will make justice [the] measuring line and righteousness [the] level; and hail will sweep away [the] refuge of lies, and waters will overflow [the] hiding place.
en.B: Justice will be my measuring line, and righteousness my plumb line. Hail will sweep away the shelter of lies, and floodwaters will swamp the hiding place.
en.R: I will use justice and righteousness like a builder's measuring line and level. Hail will sweep away the lies you hide behind. Floods will cover your hiding place.

decisions.choice: measuring line, level: the builder's tools for checking that work is straight and true
decisions.reason: God builds with the cornerstone of verse 16 and tests everything by justice and righteousness. The word for line is qav, heard in the mockery of verses 10 and 13; it now becomes the line of God's judgment (34:11; 2 Kings 21:13).

decisions.choice: hail and flood sweep away the refuge of lies
decisions.reason: The storm of verse 2 and the flooding whip of verse 15 destroy the shelter the leaders made of falsehood. Hail also recalls the battle near Gibeon (verse 21; Joshua 10:11).

decisions.choice: you hide behind; your hiding place
decisions.reason: Readable says whose refuge it is: the leaders' of verse 15.

source.text: וְכֻפַּ֤ר בְּרִֽיתְכֶם֙ אֶת־מָ֔וֶת וְחָזוּתְכֶ֥ם אֶת־שְׁא֖וֹל לֹ֣א תָק֑וּם שׁ֤וֹט שׁוֹטֵף֙ כִּ֣י יַֽעֲבֹ֔ר וִהְיִ֥יתֶם ל֖וֹ לְמִרְמָֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be covered over your covenant with death, and your agreement with Sheol not it will stand; [the] scourge overflowing, when it passes through, and you will be for it for a trampling.

en.L: And your covenant with death will be wiped out, and your pact with Sheol will not stand; [the] overflowing whip, when it passes through, you will be for it [a place of] trampling.
en.B: Your covenant with death will be wiped out, and your pact with Sheol will fail. When the flooding whip sweeps through, it will trample you into the ground.
en.R: Your agreement with death will be canceled. Your deal with the grave will not last. When disaster floods through like a whip, it will crush you.

decisions.choice: wiped out: annulled, made void
alternatives: covered over
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "cover" or "atone". Here it means to cancel or wipe out, as an agreement is annulled.

decisions.choice: you will be trampled: the boast of verse 15 reversed
decisions.reason: The leaders said the flooding whip would not reach them; it will pass through and leave them trampled, like the crown of Ephraim (verse 3).

source.text: מִדֵּ֤י עָבְרוֹ֙ יִקַּ֣ח אֶתְכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־בַבֹּ֧קֶר בַּבֹּ֛קֶר יַעֲבֹ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָיָ֥ה רַק־זְוָעָ֖ה הָבִ֥ין שְׁמוּעָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: As often as it passes through it will take you, for in the morning, in the morning it will pass through, in the day and in the night; and it will be only terror to understand [the] message.

en.L: As often as it passes through, it will seize you, for in the morning, in the morning, it will pass through, in the day and in the night; and it will be only terror to grasp [the] message.
en.B: Each time it comes through, it will seize you. It will come through every morning, by day and by night. When at last you grasp the message, it will be only terror.
en.R: It will come again and again, every morning, every day and every night, and it will carry you away. When you finally understand this message, you will be terrified.

decisions.choice: to understand the message: the message the leaders scorned
alternatives: merely hearing the report will cause terror
decisions.reason: Verse 9 asked mockingly whom the prophet could "make understand the message". The leaders will understand at last, when the invasion comes, and understanding will be nothing but terror.

decisions.choice: morning by morning: again and again, without relief
decisions.reason: The repeated phrase means every day; day and night the invader returns.

source.text: כִּֽי־קָצַ֥ר הַמַּצָּ֖ע מֵֽהִשְׂתָּרֵ֑עַ וְהַמַּסֵּכָ֥ה צָ֖רָה כְּהִתְכַּנֵּֽס׃

records.literal_gloss: For it is short the bed for stretching oneself out, and the covering it is narrow as wrapping oneself.

en.L: For the bed is short for stretching oneself out, and the covering [is] narrow for wrapping oneself.
en.B: The bed is too short for anyone to stretch out on it, and the blanket too skimpy to wrap up in.
en.R: You will be like someone with a bed too short to lie down on and a blanket too small to cover up with. Your plans will not give you rest or protection.

decisions.choice: a bed too short, a blanket too narrow: the leaders' arrangements will not give them the rest they want
decisions.reason: This sounds like a proverb. The shelter they made (verse 15) will leave them as uncomfortable and exposed as a sleeper who cannot stretch out or keep warm. It contrasts with the rest God offered (verse 12).

decisions.choice: You will be like someone ...; Your plans will not give you rest or protection.
decisions.reason: Readable says who the proverb is about and explains the picture (m1).

source.text: כִּ֤י כְהַר־פְּרָצִים֙ יָק֣וּם יְהוָ֔ה כְּעֵ֖מֶק בְּגִבְע֣וֹן יִרְגָּ֑ז לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֨הוּ֙ זָ֣ר מַעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ וְלַֽעֲבֹד֙ עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ נָכְרִיָּ֖ה עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For like [at] Mount Perazim he will rise Yahweh, like [in the] valley in Gibeon he will rage, to do his deed, strange [is] his deed, and to work his work, foreign [is] his work.

en.L: For like [at] Mount Perazim {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will rise up; like [in the] valley in Gibeon {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will rage, to do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deed, strange [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deed, and to work {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, foreign [is] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work.
en.B: As at Mount Perazim, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will stand up; as in the valley near Gibeon, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will burst into fury, to do {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deed, a strange deed, and to carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} work, an alien work.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will get up and fight, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did at Mount Perazim. He will be angry, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in the valley near Gibeon. He will do a strange thing. He will do an unexpected work.

decisions.choice: Mount Perazim and the valley at Gibeon: places where the LORD fought for Israel
decisions.reason: At Baal-perazim the LORD broke through the Philistines for David (2 Samuel 5:20; 1 Chronicles 14:11), and David struck them from Gibeon on (1 Chronicles 14:16). At Gibeon the LORD also threw down hailstones on Israel's enemies for Joshua (Joshua 10:10-14; compare verse 17).

decisions.choice: strange deed, alien work: this time the LORD fights against his own people
decisions.reason: In those battles God fought for Israel. Now he will rise up in the same way against the rulers of Jerusalem (verses 14, 22), a work that seems foreign to him.

decisions.choice: get up and fight
decisions.reason: Readable says what rising up means here (m1).

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־תִּתְלוֹצָ֔צוּ פֶּֽן־יֶחְזְק֖וּ מֽוֹסְרֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־כָלָ֨ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי מֵאֵ֨ת אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now not you should show yourselves mockers, lest they become strong your bonds; for a full end and decreed I have heard from [the] Lord Yahweh of hosts upon all the land.

en.L: And now, do not show yourselves mockers, lest your bonds be made strong; for a full end, and [one] decreed, I have heard from the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of hosts upon all the land.
en.B: Now then, give up your scoffing, or your chains will grip you harder. For I have heard from the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies of an end, complete and decreed, coming upon the whole land.
en.R: So stop mocking, or your trouble will get worse, like chains pulled tighter. The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} of Armies has told me that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has decided to destroy the whole land completely.

decisions.choice: a full end, decreed: the same words as 10:23
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats 10:22-23, where the full end decreed in the land leaves only a remnant (compare verse 5).

decisions.choice: all the land: Judah's land
alternatives: the whole earth
decisions.reason: The word can mean the whole earth or one land. Here the warning is to the rulers of Jerusalem, so the land of Judah is most likely meant, as in 10:23.

decisions.choice: your bonds be made strong: your punishment be made heavier
decisions.reason: Bonds or chains picture the judgment closing in like a captive's fetters; scoffing will only tighten them.

source.text: הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my speech.

en.L: Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my speech.
en.B: Turn your ear and hear my voice; take note and listen to what I say.
en.R: Listen to me! Hear what I am saying. Pay attention to my words.

decisions.choice: give ear, pay attention: a teacher's call to listen
decisions.reason: Wisdom teachers open a lesson this way (Proverbs 4:1; 5:1; compare Isaiah 32:9). The prophet speaks in his own voice and tells a parable about a farmer (verses 23-29).

source.text: הֲכֹ֣ל הַיּ֔וֹם יַחֲרֹ֥שׁ הַחֹרֵ֖שׁ לִזְרֹ֑עַ יְפַתַּ֥ח וִֽישַׂדֵּ֖ד אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: All the day does he plow, the plowman, to sow? Does he open and harrow his ground?

en.L: [Is it] all the day [that] the plowman plows to sow? [Does] he open and harrow his ground?
en.B: Does the farmer who plows to plant go on plowing all day long? Does he never stop breaking open and harrowing his soil?
en.R: A farmer does not spend all his time plowing so that he can plant. He does not keep on breaking up the dirt and smoothing it forever.

decisions.choice: all the day: endlessly; the question expects the answer no
decisions.reason: "All the day" means continually. Plowing and harrowing have a set time, and then the farmer moves on to sowing.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: Readable states the answer the questions expect.

source.text: הֲלוֹא֙ אִם־שִׁוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֥יץ קֶ֖צַח וְכַמֹּ֣ן יִזְרֹ֑ק וְשָׂ֨ם חִטָּ֤ה שׂוֹרָה֙ וּשְׂעֹרָ֣ה נִסְמָ֔ן וְכֻסֶּ֖מֶת גְּבֻלָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Is it not, when he has leveled its surface, and he scatters black cumin, and cumin he sprinkles, and he puts wheat [in] rows and barley [in an] appointed [place] and spelt [at] its border?

en.L: Is it not [so]: when he has leveled its surface, he scatters black cumin and sows cumin, and puts wheat [in] rows, and barley [in an] appointed [place], and spelt [at] its border?
en.B: Once he has made the ground level, does he not scatter black cumin, sow cumin seed, set wheat in rows, barley in its marked plot, and spelt along the border?
en.R: No, after he makes the ground smooth, he plants his seeds. He scatters spice seeds like black cumin and cumin. He plants wheat in rows and barley in its own place. He plants another grain, called spelt, around the edges.

decisions.choice: black cumin, cumin, spelt: crops of the land
decisions.reason: Black cumin (nigella) and cumin are small seeds used as spice. Spelt is a hardy wheat. Each crop is sown in its own way and place.

decisions.choice: in rows; in its appointed place
alternatives: millet (as a crop name)
in its proper season
decisions.reason: Both words are rare and their sense is uncertain. The first may mean "in rows" and the second "in a marked place". The point is clear: the farmer puts each seed where it belongs.

decisions.choice: No, after ...
decisions.reason: Readable answers the question of verse 24 and states the answer this question expects.

source.text: וְיִסְּר֥וֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט אֱלֹהָ֥יו יוֹרֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he instructs him for the right way; his God he teaches him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} instructs him in the right way; his God teaches him.
en.B: His God has trained him in the proper order of things and teaches him.
en.R: God teaches the farmer how to do these things. God shows him the right way.

decisions.choice: his God teaches him: the farmer's skill is God's gift
decisions.reason: The word for the right way also means "judgment" or "justice", the word of verses 6 and 17. The farmer's sense of order comes from God; so does the order of God's own dealings with his people.

source.text: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א בֶֽחָרוּץ֙ י֣וּדַשׁ קֶ֔צַח וְאוֹפַ֣ן עֲגָלָ֔ה עַל־כַּמֹּ֖ן יוּסָּ֑ב כִּ֧י בַמַּטֶּ֛ה יֵחָ֥בֶט קֶ֖צַח וְכַמֹּ֥ן בַּשָּֽׁבֶט׃

records.literal_gloss: For not with the sledge is threshed black cumin, and a wheel of a cart over cumin is turned; for with the staff is beaten out black cumin, and cumin with the rod.

en.L: For not with the threshing sledge is black cumin threshed, and a wheel of a cart over cumin [is not] turned; but with the staff black cumin is beaten out, and cumin with the rod.
en.B: No one threshes black cumin with a sledge or rolls cart wheels over cumin. Black cumin is knocked loose with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
en.R: A farmer does not use a heavy sledge to thresh black cumin. He does not roll a cart wheel over cumin seeds. He beats the seeds loose with a stick.

decisions.choice: threshing sledge, cart wheel: heavy tools for threshing grain
decisions.reason: A threshing sledge was a heavy board studded underneath with sharp stones or iron, dragged over grain on the threshing floor (41:15). Cart wheels were also driven over grain. Small seeds like cumin would be crushed by them, so they were beaten out with sticks.

source.text: לֶ֣חֶם יוּדָ֔ק כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח אָד֣וֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁ֑נּוּ וְ֠הָמַם גִּלְגַּ֧ל עֶגְלָת֛וֹ וּפָרָשָׁ֖יו לֹֽא־יְדֻקֶּֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Bread [grain] is crushed, for not forever continually does he thresh it, and he drives [the] wheel of his cart and his horses, not he crushes it.

en.L: Bread [grain] is crushed, but not forever does [one] keep threshing it; and [he] drives the wheel of his cart and his horses [over it], [but] he does not crush it [fine].
en.B: Grain for bread must be crushed, but no one keeps on threshing it endlessly. He drives the wheels of his cart and his horses over it, but he does not grind it to dust.
en.R: Wheat must be threshed to make bread. But a farmer does not keep on threshing it forever. He drives his cart and horses over it, but he does not crush the grain to powder.

decisions.choice: bread grain is crushed: a statement, with the limit that follows
alternatives: Is grain for bread crushed?
decisions.reason: The first words may be a statement ("grain is crushed") or a question ("is bread grain crushed?"). Either way the point is the next clause: threshing has a limit, and the grain is not destroyed.

decisions.choice: not forever: judgment with a purpose and a limit
decisions.reason: Threshing pictures judgment (21:10; 41:15). As the farmer threshes each crop in its own way and stops before ruining the grain, God's judgment on his people is measured and aims at a harvest, not at destruction.

decisions.choice: his horses: the animals that pull the threshing cart
alternatives: his horsemen
decisions.reason: The word can mean horses or horsemen; here, the draft animals.

source.text: גַּם־זֹ֕את מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יָצָ֑אָה הִפְלִ֣יא עֵצָ֔ה הִגְדִּ֖יל תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Also this from with Yahweh of hosts it has gone out; he has made wonderful counsel, he has made great sound wisdom.

en.L: This also has gone out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made counsel wonderful; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made wisdom great.
en.B: This too comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, whose counsel is a wonder and whose wisdom is great.
en.R: The farmer's skill also comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. His advice is wonderful. His wisdom is great.

decisions.choice: wonderful counsel: the LORD's plan, beyond human understanding
decisions.reason: The same two roots form the royal title "Wonderful Counselor" in 9:5. God's plan is marvelous (25:1), both in the farmer's craft and in his dealings with his people.

decisions.choice: wisdom: sound, effective wisdom that succeeds
decisions.reason: The word means practical wisdom that achieves its aim (Proverbs 2:7; 8:14).

decisions.choice: The farmer's skill
decisions.reason: Readable says what "this" refers to: the farmer's knowledge of verses 24-28.
